_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: One song broke the early MP3 tests.
beats.note: Everything else sounded fine. Suzanne Vega's voice was destroyed.

beats.name: Suzanne Vega
beats.role: Wrote Tom's Diner as an a cappella song, so the track is one unaccompanied voice.

beats.text: A warm, bare voice looked close to impossible to compress.
beats.note: Karlheinz Brandenburg picked it for that reason, and compared the track before and after compression.

beats.context: Brandenburg says he played the song more than 500 times while developing the technology that became the MP3.

beats.text: Audiophiles used it to check speakers.
beats.note: That began after the 1987 album Solitude Standing.

beats.text: A folk song taught a codec to hear.

beats.line: Vega is now called the Mother of the MP3.
